checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) correctly enforce the algebraic identity E(x)*Z(x) == P(x)*Z(x) over the FFT domain when processing attacker-supplied cells via P2P?

reachability.notes: An attacker providing partial cells for recovery controls which cells are available and their content. Inconsistent cells (from different polynomials) would produce an incorrect recovered polynomial.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all entry points where cell data arrives from P2P peers and flows into recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024), which calls recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023). 2. Construct a valid blob, compute its polynomial commitment (KZG), and generate all 128 cells and proofs. 3. Select exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 cells (the minimum threshold) as input. Verify that recover_polynomialcoeff produces a polynomial P(x) such that evaluating P(x) at all 128 cell coset points reproduces the original cells. 4. Now construct an ATTACK scenario: take the same 64 cells, but replace ONE cell's content with data from a DIFFERENT polynomial (simulating an attacker providing inconsistent cells). Run recovery and verify that the resulting polynomial differs from the original. 5. Critically, verify that the caller (SG-024 or the validator) re-verifies the recovered polynomial against the original KZG commitment. If this verification step is missing, the attack propagates corrupted data. 6. Verify the algebraic identity: after recovery, compute E(x)*Z(x) and P(x)*Z(x) over the full FFT domain and confirm they are equal at all points. If they differ at any point, the recovery algorithm has a bug. 7. Test with boundary cases: exactly 50% cells available, exactly 100% cells available, and various patterns of missing cells (contiguous, interleaved, random). 8. Cross-client verification: run the same recovery on at least two different Ethereum consensus client implementations (e.g., Prysm, Lighthouse, Lodestar, Nimbus, Teku) and verify they produce identical polynomial coefficients from identical inputs.

code_locations.notes: SG-023: Core recovery function. The algebraic identity E(x)*Z(x) == P(x)*Z(x) is enforced implicitly through the FFT-based polynomial division steps: (1) compute ez_eval = element-wise multiply of extended_evaluation and zero_poly_eval, (2) IFFT to get ez_coeffs, (3) coset FFT to get ez_over_coset, (4) coset FFT of zero_poly_coeff to get zp_over_coset, (5) element-wise divide ez_over_coset / zp_over_coset. Any implementation error in steps 1-5 breaks the invariant.

SG-024: Caller of recover_polynomialcoeff. Must validate inputs (cell_indices length, uniqueness, sorting, bounds) before calling recovery. The assertion checks (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 <= len(cell_indices) <= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) are the first line of defense.
SG-022: Produces Z(x) used in the algebraic identity. If Z(x) is incorrect (wrong roots, wrong degree, wrong coefficient spacing), the entire recovery fails silently.
SG-005: Performs the coset shift that avoids division by zero. shift_factor must be PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY. If the shift is wrong or coincides with a root of Z(x), division by zero occurs.

executable_checks: Property-based test: For 1000 random polynomials of degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, generate all cells, select random subsets of >= 50% cells, recover, and verify the recovered polynomial equals the original
Algebraic identity test: After recovery, explicitly compute E(x)*Z(x) and P(x)*Z(x) at all FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB points and assert equality
Adversarial cell test: Provide cells from TWO different polynomials and verify recovery produces a polynomial that does NOT match either original commitment (tests that corruption is detectable)
Cross-client differential test: Run identical recovery inputs through Prysm, Lighthouse, Nimbus, Lodestar, and Teku; assert all produce byte-identical polynomial coefficients
Minimum threshold boundary test: Recover with exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 cells and verify success; recover with CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 - 1 cells and verify rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0034, Trust Boundaries: tb-008 (Fiat-Shamir challenge for cell verification), tb-009 (internal computation boundary for validator custody). Invariants: SG-023-INV-001 (algebraic identity), SG-023-INV-002 (coset division avoids div-by-zero). The attack surface is that an attacker on P2P controls which cells are provided and their content. If the algebraic identity is violated (due to an implementation bug in FFT, IFFT, coset FFT, or element-wise operations), the recovered polynomial will be incorrect, producing wrong cells and proofs. This can cause: (1) nodes to disagree on data availability, (2) valid blobs to appear unavailable, (3) consensus divergence if different clients have different FFT implementations.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the coset division in recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) guaranteed to avoid division by zero for all possible sets of missing cell indices?

reachability.notes: An attacker providing partial cells for recovery controls which cells are available and their content. Inconsistent cells (from different polynomials) would produce an incorrect recovered polynomial.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the coset division step in recover_polynomialcoeff: `reconstructed = [a / b for a, b in zip(ez_over_coset, zp_over_coset)]`. This is where division by zero can occur if zp_over_coset contains a zero element. 2. Verify that coset_fft_field uses shift_factor = PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY (INV-001 of SG-005). 3. Verify that PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is a generator of the multiplicative group of order 2*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB, NOT a root of unity in the FFT domain. This ensures the coset {g*omega^i} does not intersect {omega^i}. 4. For each possible set of missing cell indices (or a representative sample), compute construct_vanishing_polynomial and then evaluate it on the coset via coset_fft_field. Verify that NO evaluation is zero. 5. Specifically test the adversarial case: an attacker provides exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 cells such that the missing cells have indices that maximize the degree of the vanishing polynomial. Verify that even in this worst case, the coset evaluation of Z(x) contains no zeros. 6. Test with edge cases: all even-indexed cells missing, all odd-indexed cells missing, first half missing, second half missing, alternating pattern. 7. Verify that if PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is accidentally set to a root of unity in the FFT domain (a configuration error), division by zero IS triggered -- this confirms the check is meaningful. 8. In each client implementation, verify the coset_fft_field function correctly applies the shift before FFT and that the shift_factor matches the specification constant.
checklist.bug_class: Division by Zero / Cryptographic Parameter Validation

code_locations.notes: SG-023, step q_divide: `reconstructed = [a / b for a, b in zip(ez_over_coset, zp_over_coset)]`. This is the critical division step. zp_over_coset is the coset FFT of the vanishing polynomial coefficients.

SG-005: shift_factor = PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY. INV-003 states: 'Coset avoids division by zero when dividing by vanishing polynomials'. The forward path shifts coefficients by g^i before FFT, evaluating the polynomial at {g*omega^i} instead of {omega^i}.
SG-022: Produces vanishing polynomial Z(x) with roots at missing cell evaluation points. Z(x) is zero on the FFT domain at those points but must be nonzero on the coset.

executable_checks: For all 2^7 possible patterns of 64 missing cells out of 128, compute zp_over_coset and assert no element is zero (exhaustive if feasible, or random sample of 10000 patterns)
Verify PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is not a root of unity of order FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB by checking g^FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB != 1
Negative test: set shift_factor = 1 (identity, no coset shift) and verify division by zero occurs for any non-trivial vanishing polynomial
Cross-client test: verify all clients use identical PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY value
Stress test: recover with exactly 50% cells in worst-case index patterns and verify no division by zero or panic
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0034, Trust Boundaries: tb-008, tb-009. Invariant: SG-023-INV-002 (division by Z(x) done over coset). Related: SG-005-INV-001 (shift_factor = PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY), SG-005-INV-003 (coset avoids division by zero). The coset shift is the mathematical mechanism that prevents division by zero: the vanishing polynomial Z(x) has roots at {omega^(j*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL)} for missing cell indices j, but the coset evaluation evaluates Z at {g*omega^i} which does not contain these roots (because g is not a power of omega). If any client implementation uses the wrong primitive root, uses no shift, or applies the shift in the wrong order (shift after FFT instead of before), division by zero will crash the node.

checklist.title: Verify Supporting Node: Does the recovery engine correctly construct extended_evaluation_rbo with zeros for missing cells and apply bit-reversal permutation?

reachability.notes: An attacker providing partial cells for recovery controls which cells are available and their content. Inconsistent cells (from different polynomials) would produce an incorrect recovered polynomial.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the data flow from cell input to polynomial recovery: (a) cells are converted to coset_evals via cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001), (b) an extended_evaluation_rbo array of FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB elements is constructed with zeros for missing cells and coset_evals for present cells, (c) bit_reversal_permutation is applied to get extended_evaluation. 2. Verify that the zero-filling step places zeros at the CORRECT positions. Missing cells at index j should correspond to zero evaluations at positions [j*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL : (j+1)*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL] in extended_evaluation_rbo. If the index mapping is off-by-one or uses wrong stride, the algebraic identity breaks. 3. Verify that bit_reversal_permutation is applied AFTER constructing extended_evaluation_rbo, not before. If the permutation is applied in the wrong order, the extended evaluation will not match the polynomial evaluations at roots of unity. 4. Test with a known polynomial: generate all cells, remove specific cells, run recovery, and verify the extended_evaluation after zero-filling and permutation matches the expected polynomial evaluations with zeros at missing positions. 5. Verify cross-client consistency of the bit-reversal permutation implementation. The permutation depends on the total array size being a power of 2. If different clients implement BRP differently (e.g., different bit-width assumptions), the recovery will diverge. 6. Test edge case: all cells present (no missing cells). The vanishing polynomial should be trivial (constant 1), and recovery should return the original polynomial unchanged.

code_locations.notes: SG-023, steps q_flatten and q_permute: (1) build extended_evaluation_rbo with zeros for missing cells, (2) extended_evaluation = bit_reversal_permutation(extended_evaluation_rbo). The index mapping from cell_indices to positions in extended_evaluation_rbo is critical.
Standard FFT bit-reversal. Must be consistent between encoding (SG-007 compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs) and decoding (SG-023 recovery). Inconsistency causes consensus split.

executable_checks: Round-trip test: encode a polynomial to cells via compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs, drop 50% of cells, recover via recover_polynomialcoeff, verify recovered polynomial equals original

Index mapping test: for each cell index i in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB), verify that the corresponding evaluation points in extended_evaluation_rbo are at positions [i*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL : (i+1)*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL]
BRP consistency test: verify bit_reversal_permutation(bit_reversal_permutation(x)) == x for arrays of size FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB
Cross-client BRP test: compare bit_reversal_permutation output across all consensus clients for the same input
Zero-fill verification: after building extended_evaluation_rbo with known missing indices, verify that exactly len(missing_indices)*FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements are zero
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0034, Supporting check for actor-recovery-engine. The bit-reversal permutation (BRP) is a known source of cross-client bugs in Ethereum's KZG/DAS implementation. The encoding path (SG-007) and decoding path (SG-023) must use BRP in a consistent manner. If encoding applies BRP but decoding does not (or vice versa), the recovered polynomial will be a permuted version of the original, producing valid-looking but incorrect cells. This was identified as a CRITICAL risk in the trust model analysis (stride-004, stride-011).

checklist.title: Verify Supporting Node: Does the polynomial engine correctly perform FFT, inverse FFT, and element-wise multiplication/division in the recovery pipeline?

reachability.notes: An attacker providing partial cells for recovery controls which cells are available and their content. Inconsistent cells (from different polynomials) would produce an incorrect recovered polynomial.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the full computation chain in recover_polynomialcoeff: (a) zero_poly_eval = fft_field(zero_poly_coeff, roots_ext) -- forward FFT of vanishing polynomial, (b) ez_eval = element-wise multiply of zero_poly_eval and extended_evaluation, (c) ez_coeffs = fft_field(ez_eval, roots_ext, inv=True) -- inverse FFT, (d) ez_over_coset = coset_fft_field(ez_coeffs, roots_ext) -- coset FFT, (e) zp_over_coset = coset_fft_field(zero_poly_coeff, roots_ext) -- coset FFT of vanishing poly, (f) reconstructed = element-wise divide ez_over_coset / zp_over_coset, (g) poly_coeff = coset_fft_field(reconstructed, roots_ext, inv=True) -- inverse coset FFT. 2. For each step, verify intermediate values against a reference implementation (e.g., the Python consensus-specs reference). 3. Specifically test the FFT butterfly operations: verify fft_field(fft_field(x, roots, inv=True), roots) == x (FFT/IFFT roundtrip). 4. Verify element-wise operations use BLS field arithmetic (mod BLS_MODULUS), not integer arithmetic. Integer overflow in the multiplication step (b) would corrupt the result silently. 5. Verify the inverse FFT normalization factor: fft_field with inv=True must multiply each output element by 1/N (where N = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB). If the normalization is missing or uses the wrong N, the algebraic identity breaks. 6. Test with the zero polynomial (all cells are zero) to verify recovery produces the zero polynomial. 7. Test with the identity polynomial p(x) = x to verify recovery is exact.

code_locations.notes: SG-004: Forward and inverse FFT. INV-001: inverse FFT applies normalization 1/N. INV-002: inverse FFT reverses roots_of_unity order. Bugs here affect all downstream computation.
SG-003: Recursive Cooley-Tukey FFT. INV-001: input length must be power of 2. INV-002: len(vals) == len(roots_of_unity). Butterfly operations: o[i] = x + y*root, o[i+len(L)] = x - y*root.
SG-023: Steps q_zpeval through q_icoset. Each step depends on the correctness of the previous step. A single arithmetic error propagates through the entire chain.

executable_checks: FFT roundtrip test: for 100 random polynomials, verify fft_field(fft_field(poly, roots, inv=True), roots) == poly
Coset FFT roundtrip test: verify coset_fft_field(coset_fft_field(poly, roots, inv=True), roots) == poly
Element-wise multiplication test: verify ez_eval[i] == zero_poly_eval[i] * extended_evaluation[i] (mod BLS_MODULUS) for all i
Element-wise division test: verify reconstructed[i] * zp_over_coset[i] == ez_over_coset[i] (mod BLS_MODULUS) for all i
Normalization test: verify that IFFT of FFT of [1,0,0,...,0] returns [1,0,0,...,0] (not [N,0,0,...,0])
Cross-client intermediate value comparison: at each step of recovery, compare intermediate arrays across client implementations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0034, Supporting check for actor-polynomial-engine. The recovery pipeline chains 7 algebraic operations. A single bug in any operation (wrong modular arithmetic, missing normalization, incorrect root selection, off-by-one in array indexing) silently corrupts the result. The most likely implementation bugs are: (1) integer overflow in multiplication before modular reduction, (2) missing or incorrect IFFT normalization by 1/N, (3) using wrong roots of unity (e.g., roots of order N instead of 2N), (4) incorrect butterfly operation signs (+ instead of - or vice versa).

checklist.title: Verify Post-Recovery Commitment Verification: Does the caller of recover_polynomialcoeff verify the recovered polynomial against the original KZG commitment?

reachability.notes: An attacker providing partial cells for recovery controls which cells are available and their content. Inconsistent cells (from different polynomials) would produce an incorrect recovered polynomial.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the call chain: validator receives cells via P2P -> calls recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024) -> which calls recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) -> then calls compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff to recompute all cells and proofs. 2. Critically, SG-024 does NOT internally verify the recovered polynomial against the original KZG commitment. This verification is delegated to the caller. 3. In each client implementation, verify that AFTER calling recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs, the caller performs: (a) recompute the KZG commitment from the recovered polynomial, (b) compare it with the original KZG commitment from the blob sidecar, (c) reject the recovery if the commitments do not match. 4. Test the attack scenario: an attacker provides 64 cells, where 63 are from the correct polynomial and 1 is from a different polynomial. Recovery will produce a polynomial that does not match the original commitment. Verify that the post-recovery verification catches this. 5. If the post-recovery verification is missing in any client, this is a CRITICAL vulnerability: the node will propagate corrupted cells to other peers, acting as an unwitting attack amplifier. 6. Verify that the commitment comparison uses constant-time equality (to avoid timing side channels, though this is lower priority for this specific check).
checklist.bug_class: Missing Post-Condition Verification / Defense in Depth

code_locations.notes: SG-024: Does NOT verify recovered polynomial against commitment. Returns (cells, proofs) without commitment check. The specification delegates this to the caller.
Each client must implement the post-recovery commitment verification. Check: Prysm (Go), Lighthouse (Rust), Nimbus (Nim), Lodestar (TypeScript), Teku (Java).

executable_checks: In each client, trace the code path from recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs return value to commitment verification
Adversarial recovery test: provide cells with 1 corrupted cell, recover, and verify the commitment check rejects
Missing verification test: in a test build, remove the commitment check and verify that corrupted data propagates to peers (demonstrates the attack impact)
Verify that cells recovered from an honest set of cells (all from same polynomial) pass the commitment check
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0034, Trust Boundaries: tb-008, tb-009. Related STRIDE threats: stride-004 (corrupted cells propagate without commitment check), stride-011 (node becomes vector for distributing invalid data). This check is arguably the most critical in the entire recovery pipeline: even if recover_polynomialcoeff is implemented correctly, an attacker can provide cells from a different polynomial. The algebraic identity E(x)*Z(x) == P(x)*Z(x) will still hold for the RECOVERED polynomial, but the recovered polynomial will not match the ORIGINAL polynomial. Only the KZG commitment check can detect this. Without it, the node trusts attacker-provided data unconditionally.
